profile.reading: TulsaConnect DC3, the operator's largest facility per its own site, sits at 4500 South 129th East Avenue, Tulsa, Oklahoma 74134, in the East Tulsa or Broken Arrow area. TulsaConnect's own site describes the East Tulsa building as a purpose built underground facility, located 16 feet below grade for weather protection, likely tornado resilience given Oklahoma's location in Tornado Alley, consisting of two independent data center pods each capable of housing up to 75 42U racks, for a combined 150 racks at this building alone. The operator's own site states the facility is fed by redundant A and B power feeds from two completely diverse AEP power substations, backed by on-site 800 kilowatt Caterpillar diesel generators, with redundant Eaton 9395 and Powerware 9315 UPS systems and dual substation electrical feeds; this backup generator rating is recorded here as an approximate capacity proxy rather than a marketed critical IT load figure, since TulsaConnect does not publish a specific MW rating for this building. The operator states the facility is SSAE 16 audited with biometric access control. TulsaConnect describes itself on its own site as Oklahoma's oldest and most experienced locally owned provider of data center and managed service provider services, with operations dating back to 1996, and states company wide it operates three geographically diverse data centers with an aggregate capacity of over 400 racks, of which this DC3 building's 150 racks form the largest single share. This registry's own earlier contact page cross reference found the same street address serving as the company's main office, consistent with the office being co-located with this primary data center building. Tulsa sits outside the primary US hyperscale corridors but has drawn locally owned providers like TulsaConnect by serving Oklahoma and regional Midwest enterprise, healthcare, and government customers who prioritize in-state data residency and local support relationships over the lowest possible price point available from larger national wholesale operators, a common positioning for community and regionally focused colocation providers tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
TulsaConnect DC3 publishes no power capacity, square footage, or IT load specifications, making its scale relative to AI infrastructure impossible to determine from available sources.

Oklahoma has nine mapped data center facilities on record, and none publish power capacity figures. TulsaConnect DC3 ranks first in the state by published megawatts only because all Oklahoma facilities withhold this data. The ranking reflects absence of disclosure rather than confirmed capacity or performance advantage.

The operator has operated since 1996 and describes itself as Oklahoma's oldest locally owned data center provider. Whether this facility is configured for high-density compute workloads, what certifications it holds, what power and cooling it can deliver to tenants, or whether it participates in AI infrastructure at all remain unknown. Without published specifications, the facility cannot be assessed as a factor in compute availability or AI scaling.
